title: CISA warns admins to immediately fix Ivanti flaw exploited as zero-day
summary: A security flaw in Ivanti Connect Secure software is being actively exploited by attackers in the wild. Organizations must apply updates immediately to prevent unauthorized access.

also_covered.title: CISA Urges Immediate Ivanti Connect Secure Updates as Honeypots Log 105 Exploit Attempts

action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything. If your workplace uses Ivanti Connect Secure, your IT team should already be on it.
action_it: Immediately update your Ivanti Connect Secure (ICS) appliances and deployments to the latest version provided by the vendor.

title: Microsoft Patches Record 1,413 Flaws, Including Exploited Windows Shell Bug
summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking number of software updates to fix over 1,400 security flaws, including at least one that is currently being exploited by attackers. These updates protect against malicious takeovers and unauthorized access across Windows and other Microsoft products.

also_covered.title: Microsoft Patches More Than 1,400 Security Flaws
Microsoft October 2026 Patch Tuesday fixes 1,411 flaws, 3 zero-days

action_everyone: Install the latest Windows and Microsoft updates today to protect your devices from actively targeted security flaws. Go to Settings > Windows Update > Check for updates.
action_it: Apply Microsoft's October updates across all affected systems immediately, prioritizing the actively exploited Windows Shell vulnerability.

title: curl Patches HTTP/2 Upload Flaw After PoC Demonstrates Client-Side Code Execution
summary: A security flaw in curl could let a malicious server corrupt memory and run harmful code when a user uploads data over HTTP/2. The curl project has released a fix in version 8.23.0.
action_everyone: Most people don't need to do anything right away, but you should update your software and tools when updates become available.
action_it: Upgrade curl to version 8.23.0 to apply the patch.

title: Hirudo Android Trojan Uses Patched Banking Apps to Bypass Their Built-In Security Checks
summary: A new malicious Android app called Hirudo steals banking login details by swapping real banking applications with modified versions that disable built-in security checks. This targets users of at least eight Indonesian banking apps.

also_covered.title: Hirudo Android malware replaces banking apps to evade security checks

action_everyone: Only download apps from official app stores like Google Play, and be very careful about giving apps extra permissions or installing apps from unfamiliar websites. If you use any Indonesian banking apps, ensure your device's security software is up to date and watch out for any unexpected requests to reinstall your apps.

title: AI-Found Linux Kernel Flaw Gives Local Users Root, and Can Break a Guest Out to the Host
summary: A serious security flaw in the Linux operating system kernel lets local users gain full control of a system and can allow virtual machines to escape to the host computer. This bug affects software used by businesses, cloud providers, and advanced users over the last ten years.
action_everyone: Most people do not need to do anything. If your workplace or cloud provider uses Linux virtualization, your IT team will need to apply the necessary updates.
action_it: Apply vendor patches for CVE-2026-74580 as soon as they become available to prevent local privilege escalation and guest-to-host escapes in the vhost subsystem.

title: Researchers Used a Public OpenAI Model to Build a $250,000 Chrome Full-Chain Exploit in Six Days
summary: Security researchers used a public artificial intelligence model to quickly chain three Google Chrome browser bugs into a powerful attack that runs malicious code just by visiting a web page. Google has already fixed all three security flaws.

title: An AI Agent Found a Critical OTP Bypass in Production. The Attack Was the Easy Part.
summary: An artificial intelligence security testing agent discovered a major flaw in a live insurance website that let users redirect login codes. This discovery highlights the growing capability of automated tools to find critical website security holes.

title: Microsoft: Recent Windows updates may trigger Remote Desktop failures
summary: Recent Windows updates can block regular users from connecting to devices via Remote Desktop if a specific security setting is turned on. This matters because it may lock non-administrator users out of their remote connections.

title: Microsoft fixes VPN issues caused by September Windows updates
summary: Microsoft has fixed an issue where September Windows 11 updates broke certain virtual private network (VPN) connections. This matters because affected users could not connect securely to their networks until the issue was resolved.

title: Four-Byte Write and Timing Bug Let Researchers Run Code in Windows SmartScreen Enclave
summary: Researchers successfully ran unauthorized code inside a protected, highly secure part of Windows used to guard sensitive data like passwords. This was done in a laboratory setting to demonstrate the flaw, meaning there is no active attack happening right now.

title: U.S. Shuts Down Over 40 Laptop Farms, Charges 14 in North Korean IT Worker Fraud
summary: The U.S. Department of Justice charged 14 people and seized nearly 190 computers involved in a North Korean remote IT worker fraud scheme. This matters because it disrupts a major illicit operation that placed hidden foreign workers into over 70 U.S. companies.

title: U.K. Sanctions Cryptomus for RU Money Laundering
summary: The U.K. has placed financial sanctions on Cryptomus, a cryptocurrency platform used to launder money and help Russia bypass financial restrictions. This move aims to cut off a major financial channel for cybercriminals, ransomware gangs, and illicit darknet markets.

title: The Blind Spots of Agentic Pentesting and How to Close Them
summary: AI-powered penetration testing helps find security flaws, but safety rules and network limits can leave some weaknesses hidden. Combining AI testing with other simulation tools can help security teams find and close these gaps.

title: Global takedown hits network behind 1 billion phishing messages
summary: Law enforcement agencies worldwide have disrupted a massive cybercrime network responsible for sending over a billion phishing messages. This takedown significantly reduces a major infrastructure used to target organizations globally.

title: How to Run a Deepfake Readiness Drill Before a Cloned Voice Calls Your Team
summary: Security teams are running simulated drills using artificial voice cloning and video to test how well their staff can spot fraud. This matters because scammers are increasingly using these deepfake technologies to trick employees into making unauthorized payments or resetting accounts.
